plot: On their prize camping night in the garden, a secret rain soaks only Max's tent under a clear sky and follows them when they move it; Max reasons it comes from the grass, finds a spinning sprinkler and realises his own beep on Grandma's grey flower-timer box started it, so he reads the buttons, switches it off, owns up, and they see the first star before Grandma promises to teach him her old scooter tomorrow.

beats.say: Pssht! Water! Run, Bird, run! It's raining on our tent!
My feathers! My snacks! Everything is wet! Tweet!
Why is it raining only on us? The sky is clear!
One hour ago, everything was perfect.
It's camping night in the garden. The prize from the pet show!
Our very first night outside! No beds, no sofa!
I brought a flashlight, a blanket, and nine cookies!
Nine? Last time you said lots. Nine is lots.
A tent needs a light. Where is the light switch out here?
Max finds a little grey box by the roses.
It has a big green button. Max presses it. Beep!
Hmm. No light. Silly box. Never mind!
Max! Grandma said that box is for her flowers.
Flowers? It's just a box. Come on, it's camping time!
Wait for me! I brought my pillow! And my other pillow!
The sun goes down. The sky turns orange, then purple.
Dog yawns the biggest yawn in the whole garden.
Dog! You can't sleep yet! We didn't eat cookies!
Not sleeping. Just resting my eyes. Very, very hard.
Let's count the first stars. Whoever sees one first wins!
Everybody lies down on the soft grass and looks up.
Then from the dark grass comes a tiny sound. Tick. Tick. Tick.
Did you hear that? Something is ticking near the roses.
Maybe it's a cricket. Crickets love camping too.
And that's when the secret rain began.
Back to now. Max, Bird and Dog hide under the blanket.
I'm awake! Who poured water on my pillow? Both pillows!
Our camping night is ruined before the first star!
We have to stop this rain. But how do you stop rain?
Easy! We move the tent. Rain can't find us over there!
Everybody pulls the tent to the far side of the garden.
Ha! Dry grass! Dry tent! Goodbye, silly rain!
They wait. One second. Two seconds. Three.
The rain turns slowly, slowly... and finds them again! Splash!
It's following us! This rain has eyes!
My pillows are soup now. Pillow soup.
Let's fly away to the roof! Oh. You can't fly. Sorry!
If it keeps raining, we sleep inside. No camping. No stars!
Max is cold and wet. But now he gets curious.
Wait. Real rain falls from the sky. Look at the clouds.
There are no clouds. Only stars coming out.
So this rain is coming from... down there. From the grass!
Max crawls through the wet grass. Drip, drip on his nose.
And there it is. A little blue thing, spinning and spraying.
A sprinkler! It turns round and round. That's why it followed us!
A sprinkler? Who turns on a sprinkler at night?
Max thinks. Tick, tick. Beep. The little grey box.
Oh no. The green button. Beep. That was me.
The flower box! It's a timer. It waters the garden.
I wanted a light. I turned on the rain instead!
So the secret rain was Max all along? Tweet!
Okay. I started it. So I will stop it.
Max runs to the grey box. Splash, splash, through the puddles.
This time he doesn't press any button. He reads the little words.
Green says ON. Red says OFF. Red it is!
Beep. The sprinkler slows down. Tick... tick... stop.
My goodness! Why is everyone so wet?
I pressed your flower button, Grandma. I'm sorry.
Thank you for telling me, dear. And for fixing it.
Now, who wants a warm, dry towel?
Grandma rubs everyone dry. Max's fur sticks up like a lion.
Look! Up there! The first star! I saw it first!
Everyone lies on the dry blanket and looks at the star.
Read before you press. And if you make a mess, fix it.
Stars are nice. But cookies are nicer. Are the cookies dry?
Dog is the first one asleep. Snoring on two soggy pillows.
Max, look. Grandma left her old blue scooter by the gate.
Tomorrow I'll teach you to ride it. If you're brave enough.
A scooter? Me? With four paws? This will be wobbly!
